summary: Russian forces continued strikes across Ukraine overnight, hitting Odesa, Kharkiv, and Zhytomyr regions with casualties and infrastructure damage reported. Ukraine's President Zelenskyy announced plans for new diplomatic and air defense contacts this week. Protests erupted in 22 Polish cities against violence targeting Ukrainians, with over 11,000 signatures collected for a petition to the Polish government.
key_points: Russian overnight strikes hit Odesa, Kharkiv, and Zhytomyr regions with casualties and infrastructure damage reported. (Source: @UkraineNow/83328)
In Odesa, 8 people were injured in a Russian attack; a four-story residential building caught fire, and two private homes burned. (Source: @UkraineNow/83315)
In Kharkiv, 12 people were reported injured following Russian attacks. (Source: @UkraineNow/83315)
Ukraine's President Zelenskyy announced new diplomatic and air defense contacts planned for the coming week. (Source: @UkraineNow/83328)
Protests against violence targeting Ukrainians took place in 22 Polish cities, with over 11,000 signatures collected for a petition to the Polish government. (Source: @UkraineNow/83326)
Russian forces destroyed a C-400 air defense system position in Gelendzhik and struck four additional air defense elements and three Black Sea Fleet vessels. (Source: @UkraineNow/83311)
Ukrainian drones attacked the Turkish bulk carrier MV Reyhan Sarı off Novorossiysk on July 22, leading to an ICC lawsuit filed by the ship's owner. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32318)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces continue systematic strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure and civilian areas, with recent attacks causing casualties in Odesa and Kharkiv. The destruction of a C-400 system and Black Sea Fleet vessels indicates ongoing naval and air defense engagements. Ballistic missile threats remain elevated over Kyiv and surrounding regions. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries and port infrastructure suggest reciprocal escalation. The involvement of international actors, including Turkey and Germany, highlights the expanding scope of the conflict.
sections.regional_response: Polish citizens organized protests in 22 cities against violence targeting Ukrainians, collecting over 11,000 signatures for a petition to the Polish government. Turkey's Foreign Minister called for a mechanism to impose a moratorium on attacks against commercial ships in the Black Sea. Germany is likely to respond only with formal measures regarding the Nord Stream pipeline incident. International shipping companies, including Turkish operators, are increasingly affected by the conflict's reach into the Black Sea.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian forces are systematically targeting port infrastructure in the Greater Odessa region, including Chornomorsk, Yuzhny, Nikolaev, and Danube ports, to disrupt maritime trade. Strikes on logistics centers in Kiev and surrounding areas indicate a broader campaign against supply chains. Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries and marketplaces suggest efforts to degrade economic capacity. The involvement of international legal mechanisms, such as the ICC lawsuit filed by the Turkish shipowner, reflects the conflict's global implications. Continued escalation in both kinetic and diplomatic domains is expected.
